chunks: My father (may God have mercy on him) narrated to us. He said: 'Abdullah ibn Ja'far al-Himyari narrated to us from Ahmad ibn Muhammad ibn 'Isa, from his father, from Yunus ibn 'Abd al-Rahman, from Mansur al-Sayqal, from al-Sadiq Ja'far ibn Muhammad, from his forefathers (peace be upon them). He said:

The Messenger of God (peace be upon him and his family) said: When I was taken on the Night Journey to heaven, my Lord enjoined upon me three phrases regarding Ali. He said: 'O Muhammad!' I said: 'I am at Your service, my Lord.' He said: 'Indeed, Ali is the Imam of the God-fearing, the leader of the bright-faced and radiant-limbed, and the chief of the believers.'

key_terms.أُسْرِيَ بِي: I was taken (on the Isra', the Night Journey)
key_terms.الْغُرِّ الْمُحَجَّلِينَ: those with bright faces and radiant limbs (from wudu and prayer)
key_terms.يَعْسُوبُ: chief, master, commander (originally the king bee — used to denote supreme leadership)

ai.seo_question: What did God say to the Prophet Muhammad about Imam Ali during the Night Journey (Mi'raj)?
ai.summary: This hadith recounts the Prophet Muhammad's Night Journey (Mi'raj) to heaven, during which God directly addressed him with three divine declarations about Imam Ali (AS). The three titles conferred upon Ali — Imam of the God-fearing, Leader of those radiant with the mark of their prayers and ablutions, and Chief of the believers — represent a divine appointment of extraordinary authority. For the original audience of Shia Muslims in 4th century AH Qum, these words served as a foundational proof text for the divine legitimacy of Imam Ali's leadership, carrying particular weight as a direct divine speech heard by the Prophet during the most exalted moment of his prophethood.
